thread:
Alex K: just finished canary deploy of release v1.23.4 to 5% (deploy-id: r2026-0315-7a9). putting monitoring on it for 10m.
IncidentBot: ALERT: canary /v1/generate error-rate > 10% over baseline (threshold 5%). triggered at 1775123460.
Maya R: i'm getting paged, looking now. any idea what changed?
Alex K: it's the routing tweak for model selection (commit abc1234). small change but touched stream fallback.
Sam L: logs show a spike of 502s from the stream proxy for canary nodes. stacktrace points to streaming connection close after first chunk.
Maya R: can we rollback the commit quickly? is it safe to revert the single commit?
Alex K: yes it's a single change that added a header check. revert should be safe. i can do it if ops approves.
Tessa J: ops - do we want a full rollback or a hotfix revert commit? canary only but we should be conservative.
Sam L: hotfix revert (git revert abc1234) + redeploy to canary then promote if healthy. avoids touching other commits.
Maya R: agreed. i'll take oncall for this one, coordinating the revert and deploy.
Maya R: @OpsBot please lower canary traffic to 2% while we test revert.
OpsBot: command accepted: set-canary --percent 2 --deploy r2026-0315-7a9 (user: Maya R)
Alex K: preparing revert now.
Alex K: running:
```
# revert the bad commit and push
git checkout main
git pull origin main
git revert --no-edit abc1234
git push origin main
```
Alex K: created revert commit def5678 and pushed. CI pipeline started (pipeline id: ci-8891).
IncidentBot: CI pipeline ci-8891 status: started.
Maya R: once CI passes, trigger canary deploy of revert commit def5678 at 2%.
Sam L: quick check: does this revert need any DB migration? no. just routing header logic.
Tessa J: I'll keep customer-facing comms ready in case it broadens.
IncidentBot: CI pipeline ci-8891 status: passed.
Alex K: promoting revert to canary: deploy-tool promote --sha def5678 --env prod --canary 2 --deploy-id r2026-0315-7a9-revert
OpsBot: deploy started: r2026-0315-7a9-revert (canary 2%).
Maya R: watching metrics. please paste p99/err graphs if you have them.
Sam L: past 3m: canary 502s dropped from 11.8% -> 2.1% within 90s of new canary pods warmup.
Alex K: logs look clean, streaming connections stable.
Tessa J: customer impact assessment: no paid customer incidents reported; errors only from canary traffic and internal test agents. low business impact.
Maya R: roll to 10% for confidence, continue to monitor; if stable, promote to 50% then full.
OpsBot: set-canary --percent 10 --deploy r2026-0315-7a9-revert (user: Maya R) -- done
Sam L: at 10% p95 latency steady, errors ~1.2% (baseline).
Alex K: promoting to 50% now.
OpsBot: set-canary --percent 50 --deploy r2026-0315-7a9-revert (user: Maya R) -- done
Maya R: ok at 50% looks good. promote to full.
Alex K: full rollout initiated.
OpsBot: rollout complete. all nodes on def5678.
Maya R: monitors green. closing the incident.
Tessa J: filing post-deploy hotfix ticket and short RCA. action: add integration test for streaming header case, add a canary abort playbook.
Sam L: assigning to Alex K and Maya R for followup.
Alex K: thanks everyone. cc @IncidentBot please annotate deploy id r2026-0315-7a9 with incident note 'reverted abc1234 -> def5678 due to streaming 502s on canary'
IncidentBot: note added to deploy r2026-0315-7a9.
Maya R: final impact summary: canary-only regressions, no customer-facing outages, resolved via single-commit revert and redeploy within ~8 minutes from alert.
Tessa J: nice recovery. will draft comms template in #product-liaison if needed. :thumbsup:
